title: Prompt Regimen Mini-Journal
content:
Purpose:
This is a personal scratch/journal for experimenting with a small, composable prompt regimen designed to keep model behavior temporally consistent across user sessions and across instruction drift. Not intended for productization yet — just notes, short experiments, few-shot sets, and failure case hunting.

High-level hypothesis:
- Models tend to "forget" or drift when prompts rely on relative temporal language ("recently", "last week") or when instructions change slightly between turns. A lightweight regimen that mixes explicit date anchors, short exemplars, and an incremental reminder at N-turns can reduce hallucination about time and preserve instruction fidelity.

Quick experiment log:
- 2024-11-12: initial idea sketched after noticing user complaints about assistant giving stale "company policy" dates.
- 2024-12-02: ran small A/B with gpt-ish open model (locally hosted) — +15% accuracy on "when did X happen" questions when date-anchor included.
- 2025-03-19: tried 2-shot vs 4-shot; found diminishing returns after 3 exemplars for latency-sensitive contexts.
- 2026-02-17: repro on larger context windows: still wins but need to limit exemplar length to <120 tokens to avoid token budget blowout.

Regimen building blocks (draft components):
1) Date-anchor header (always present for time-sensitive flows)
   - Format: [TODAY: YYYY-MM-DD | TIMEZONE: PDT]
   - Example: [TODAY: 2026-02-20 | TZ: America/Los_Angeles]

2) Short instruction goal (1 line)
   - Ex: "Goal: summarize the policy change in 2 bullets (preserve exact dates)."

3) 2–3 micro-exemplars (concise; demonstrate correct temporal phrasing)
   - Exemplar format (compact):
     Q: "When did the policy switch take effect?"
     A: "Effective 2025-09-15 (ISO)."

4) One-line fallback behavior spec (if uncertain, ask user instead of guessing)
   - Ex: "If date unknown, ask: 'Do you have the policy doc or a date reference?'"

Template (combined):
[HEADER] [TODAY: 2026-02-20 | TZ: America/Los_Angeles]
Goal: {goal}
Exemplars:
Q1: {short question}
A1: {short correct answer}
Q2: {short question}
A2: {short correct answer}
Constraint: keep answers <= 40 tokens; if unsure ask clarifying q.

Micro-shot bank (examples to rotate in experiments):
- Q: "When did we deprecate v1 API?"
  A: "2024-08-01 (deprecation announced 2024-06-15)."
- Q: "What is the date of the last roadmap update?"
  A: "Updated 2025-11-05; see release notes."
- Q: "Has the pricing changed this quarter?"
  A: "No pricing change recorded for Q4 2025."

Failure cases noticed (notes / triage):
- Relative language slip: model answers with relative times ("two months ago") and those relative anchors drift across sessions. Root cause: no explicit anchor in prompt; model computes relative offset from model-internal "now" (which can be non-deterministic in our setup).
- Overfitting to exemplars: when exemplar wording too similar to target question, model parrots exemplar specifics (wrong date copied). Hypothesis: exemplar length >> target leads to copying artifacts.
- Token budget blow-up: concatenating many exemplars + large header increases cost; need cap (recommend <3 exemplars and 120 tokens total for few-shot region).
- Too-chatty fallback: if fallback instruction is too polite/long, model generates clarification plus extraneous 2–3 sentences. Fix: hard constraint — single question only.

Mini experiments (results summary):
- Anchored vs unanchored (n=120 queries): anchored reduced absolute-date hallucinations from 22% -> 7%.
- 1-shot vs 3-shot (n=60): 1-shot latency wins but accuracy drop ~6%; 3-shot sweet spot for accuracy-sensitive surfaces.
- Explicit-iso vs natural language date (n=80): ISO dates (YYYY-MM-DD) have higher exact-match recall.

Example prompt for prod-prototype (short):
[HEADER] [TODAY: 2026-02-20 | TZ: America/Los_Angeles]
Goal: provide an exact date or ask for source.
Q: "When did the security policy change to require MFA?"
Ex1: Q: "When did we require MFA?" A: "2025-01-26 (policy effective)."
Constraint: answer with date only or ask for doc.

Observed model output (bad):
- "I think it was about a year ago, probably in January."  <-- ambiguous / bad

Desired model output (good):
- "2025-01-26."  <-- precise + ISO

Open questions / experiments to run next:
- How does this regimen behave under streaming responses? Does the model drop the header earlier in the token buffer? (schedule: run with streaming on small cohort)
- Can we auto-generate compact exemplars from a canonical dataset of timeline items? (prefilter by token length)
- Evaluate cadence: insert header every N turns vs only at session start. Best tradeoff between statefulness and token cost?
- Test with quantized/edge models — does quantization amplify copying/overfitting issues?

Notes to self / TODOs:
- [ ] Build small script to synthesize 500 short exemplars from company timeline and filter by token length + diversity (sketch: python pipeline, use embedding clustering to pick 3 per cluster).
- [ ] Open GitHub issue linking to PROJ-301 with sample failing prompts + references. (assigned Marco?)
- [ ] Try hybrid: header + single exemplar + very strict constraint: "one-line answer, date only" and measure user-perceived helpfulness.
- [ ] Draft short internal doc for solutions-engineering: "Temporal prompt regimen: quickstart" (keep to single page).

Random heuristics discovered (keep):
- Always prefer ISO date when exactness matters.
- Limit exemplar variance: vary phrasing but keep answer format consistent (ISO).
- Use explicit fallback instruction to avoid confident hallucinations.
- If token budget is tight, prefer header + 1 exemplar rather than 3 exemplars.

Snippets to iterate on (copyable):
HEADER = "[TODAY: {today} | TZ: {tz}]"
MICRO_PROMPT = "Goal: {goal}\nEx1: Q: {q1}\nA: {a1}\nEx2: Q: {q2}\nA: {a2}\nConstraint: answer with ISO date YYYY-MM-DD or ask one clarifying question."

Session notes: 2026-02-20 noon session: model still occasionally outputs human-ish clarifications. Shortening the constraint line to be more imperative ("Respond with ISO date or ask one question.") reduced verbosity.

End of entry. Back to experiments tomorrow.

---
Meta: if this matures, migrate to shared_drives/product/hosted-api/prompt-regimens/ for peer review and add an evaluation harness (rubric: exact-date recall, dialog-turn cost, user satisfaction).
